reason: Cool rock should let rain reach and remain on the ground.

effect: Rain remains liquid on the cool rock, completing the chapter and making accumulation in low ground possible.
reaction: It is satisfying to see why rain can persist on one patch while nearby lava remains hot.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the coast was most worthwhile: the contrast between cool rock and nearby lava made uneven heat loss and water retention clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Bringing droplets down with gravity felt like a predictable progression, although the note about evaporation added useful context.

surprise.text: Rain could evaporate in hot air or boil on landing, so clouds and rainfall alone do not guarantee standing water.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the offered combinations had clear physical purposes.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how water accumulating in low ground develops into a sea, though the mostly predictable choices offer limited challenge.
